instruction:

df["city"].value_counts()

FROM residents
GROUP BY city
ORDER BY count DESC;

instruction:

df.query("age > 25 and city == 'Paris'")

Convert this pandas aggregation to SQL:

df.agg({"salary": "mean", "age": "max"})
output:
SELECT AVG(salary) AS salary, MAX(age) AS age
FROM employees;

instruction:
Convert this pandas isin filter to SQL:

df[df["status"].isin(["active", "pending"])]

Convert this pandas fillna to SQL:

df.fillna({"score": 0, "city": "unknown"})
output:
SELECT COALESCE(score, 0) AS score, COALESCE(city, 'unknown') AS city
FROM results;

instruction:
Convert this pandas pivot_table to SQL:

df.pivot_table(index="dept", columns="gender", values="salary", aggfunc="mean")
output:
SELECT dept,
  AVG(CASE WHEN gender = 'F' THEN salary END) AS F,
  AVG(CASE WHEN gender = 'M' THEN salary END) AS M
FROM employees
GROUP BY dept;
